input: What is a deadlock in DBMS?
actual_output: Good question, Kaustubh! A deadlock happens when two or more transactions each hold a lock the other one needs, so they wait on each other forever. For example, T1 locks row A and waits for row B, while T2 locks row B and waits for row A. The DBMS usually detects this with a wait-for graph and aborts one of the transactions to break the cycle.
